method.description: A position paper that categorizes accident risks by where in the design process things go wrong, illustrates them with a fictional office-cleaning robot, reviews prior work, and proposes research directions with proposals for experiments for each of the five problems.

passages.text:
Our goal in this document is to highlight a few concrete safety problems that are ready for experimentation today and relevant to the cutting edge of AI systems, as well as reviewing existing
literature on these problems. In Section 2, we frame mitigating accident risk (often referred to as
“AI safety” in public discussions) in terms of classic methods in machine learning, such as supervised
classification and reinforcement learning. We explain why we feel that recent directions in machine
learning, such as the trend toward deep reinforcement learning and agents acting in broader environments, suggest an increasing relevance for research around accidents. In Sections 3-7, we explore five
concrete problems in AI safety. Each section is accompanied by proposals for relevant experiments.
Section 8 discusses related efforts, and Section 9 concludes.

We can categorize safety problems according to where in the process things went wrong.
First, the designer may have specified the wrong formal objective function, such that maximizing that
objective function leads to harmful results, even in the limit of perfect learning and infinite data.

stated_hypotheses: Accident risk is framed in terms of practical issues with modern machine learning techniques (such as supervised classification and reinforcement learning) rather than extreme scenarios about superintelligent agents.

setting.systems: Modern machine learning systems, including reinforcement learning agents, illustrated with a fictional office-cleaning robot

limits.notes: The passages offer a categorization, a literature review and proposals for experiments, not results.

strength.reason: A research agenda and categorization; the passages contain proposals for experiments but no experiment or proof supporting the claim.

method.description: A conceptual argument within the semi-supervised reinforcement learning framing, illustrated with the cleaning robot: an agent whose true reward is a sparse detailed human evaluation could learn cheaper proxies, and would be incentivized to seek proxy feedback rather than break the link between the user's reaction and the real reward.

stated_hypotheses: The agent's true reward is a reliable detailed human evaluation that is available only sparsely.
The agent wants as much cheap proxy feedback as it can get about whether its decisions will ultimately receive high reward.

setting.systems: A reinforcement learning agent in semi-supervised RL, illustrated by the fictional cleaning robot
setting.judge: A human whose detailed evaluation gives the sparse true reward
